scope: For arbitrary real two-by-two matrices with nonzero traces of A, B, and F, the four equalities FA=BE, GA=AF, EB=BF, FB=AG and det(F)=0 imply AB=BA. This pure matrix theorem needs no positivity or determinant hypotheses on A or B. For a nonnegative real affine reversed certificate with either eligible strict outer gap, mixed-word growth gives F squared nonzero, so det(F)=0 forces a positive trace of F. If both binary traces are nonzero and the aggregate of all five digit matrices has positive return paths between every pair of coordinates, the checked return-path equalities and ordered-binary obstruction then force det(F) nonzero. The return-path and binary-trace hypotheses are essential to this stated corollary and have not been removed. There are no inner-offset, readout normalization, or coefficient-cap assumptions. This is a conditional certificate obstruction, not a proof of Collatz.
